summary: Turn 16. The turn-15 exploration executed in the clean copy (CheckRun 8933f1bb9e8b452ca7b10f5bfbf24c60, exit 0) and produced a deterministic observation for the durability Candidate: with Durable=true and an os.Pipe StableStore, an instance with bal=7, vbal=2, Status=ACCEPTED(3), Seq=5 and Deps=[-1,-1,-1] yielded a 21-byte record whose first four bytes are 2 (vbal), with status 3 and seq 5, and the harness reported bal_persisted=false and vbal_persisted_at_bal_slot=true. That corroborates the source reading that recordInstanceMetadata's first PutUint32 is overwritten by the second, so inst.bal is never persisted. On that basis I formed a single obligation rather than a check, because the requirement still lacks a normative source and no replay reader exists in the captured files. Submitted action=obligation continuing candidate 2347fc91e49249aa8fca5330bbed6102, with claim CLM-DURABLE-BAL ('for any instance whose bal and vbal differ, the durable metadata record must carry bal in its own field, distinct from vbal, so the record can distinguish the current ballot from the pre-accept ballot'), an explicit Scope (Durable=true writes in package epaxos; non-durable runs and restart semantics excluded), pending items (which material establishes the requirement; whether a restart reader exists), Grounding with derivation, applicability, unresolved and alternatives, and one binding BND-DURABLE-WRITE (material S-DURABLE-META, symbol recordInstanceMetadata, lines 199-215) associated to the claim. Counterevidence and unknowns keep it honest: Durable is false by default, no reader was found, and the record still carries status/seq/deps. Preflight validation returns valid=true; formal acceptance and any execution remain the controller's.
